ourClaims.timeToEffect: 2–4 weeks for anxiety/stress; 4–8 weeks for cognitive effects
ourClaims.studySummary: A 2019 RCT (Choudhary et al.) found KSM-66 at 300mg twice daily significantly improved memory, attention, and information processing speed versus placebo over 8 weeks. A 2012 RCT showed 27.9% reduction in cortisol. KSM-66 has the most clinical trials of any ashwagandha extract (>24 gold-standard studies).

humanEffects.notes: 27.9% cortisol reduction (Chandrasekhar 2012) is one of the largest effect sizes in the adaptogen literature.
Consistently significant in both clinical anxiety populations and healthy high-stress subjects.
Reduces sleep latency and improves sleep quality ratings, likely via GABA modulation and cortisol reduction.
Memory and processing speed improvements are most pronounced in stressed or sleep-deprived subjects, not rested baseline.

howToTake.timing: Evening (1–2 hours before bed) for sleep benefits. Morning for cortisol and stress management. Split dosing (300mg AM + 300mg PM) is used in the most comprehensive trials.
howToTake.withFood: Take with food to minimise GI upset (particularly with 600mg doses). Absorption is not significantly affected by food.
howToTake.forms: Capsule. Insist on KSM-66 (full-spectrum root extract, 5% withanolides) or Sensoril (leaf + root, 8% withanolides, lower dose needed). Avoid unstandardised ashwagandha with no withanolide percentage stated — active content may be negligible.

studies.title: A prospective, randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled study of safety and efficacy of a high-concentration full-spectrum extract of ashwagandha root in reducing stress and anxiety in adults.
studies.extract: KSM-66 (Ixoreal Biomed) — confirmed by name in full text
studies.result: Full-text verified: serum cortisol fell 27.9% from baseline in the ashwagandha group vs 7.9% in placebo (between-group p=0.002); PSS fell 44.0% vs 5.5% (p<0.0001)
studies.fundingConflict: Extract (KSM-66) supplied by Ixoreal Biomed; sponsor role in study design not disclosed in text

studies.title: Effects of Ashwagandha (Withania Somnifera) on stress and anxiety: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
studies.outcome: Perceived Stress Scale, Hamilton Anxiety Scale, serum cortisol
studies.result: Significant pooled effect vs placebo: PSS MD -4.72 (95% CI -8.45 to -0.99); HAS MD -2.19 (95% CI -3.83 to -0.55); cortisol MD -2.58 (95% CI -4.99 to -0.16)

studies.title: Efficacy and Safety of Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera (L.) Dunal) Root Extract in Improving Memory and Cognitive Functions.
studies.population: adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) — NOT healthy adults
studies.extract: not branded as KSM-66 in the abstract; described only as ashwagandha-root extract
studies.outcome: Wechsler Memory Scale III subtests, executive function tasks
studies.result: Significant improvements in immediate and general memory (WMS-III logical memory, verbal paired associates, faces, family pictures, all p<0.05) and executive function/attention/processing speed tasks

studies.title: Examining the effect of Withania somnifera supplementation on muscle strength and recovery: a randomized controlled trial.
studies.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
studies.outcome: 1-RM strength, muscle size, testosterone, creatine kinase
studies.result: Significantly greater strength gains (bench press +46.0kg vs +26.4kg, p=0.001), muscle size, and testosterone increase (+96.2 ng/dL vs +18.0 ng/dL, p=0.004) vs placebo

studies.title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Study Examining the Hormonal and Vitality Effects of Ashwagandha in Aging, Overweight Males.
studies.population: overweight men aged 40-70 with mild fatigue
studies.duration: 8 weeks per crossover arm (16 weeks total)
studies.outcome: salivary DHEA-S, testosterone, cortisol, estradiol; mood/vigor questionnaires
studies.result: DHEA-S +18% (p=.005) and testosterone +14.7% (p=.010) vs placebo; NO significant between-group difference in cortisol, estradiol, fatigue, vigor, or sexual well-being

studies.title: Herb-Induced Liver Injury by Ayurvedic Ashwagandha as Assessed for Causality by the Updated RUCAM: An Emerging Cause.
studies.population: 2 new cases (36-year-old man, 30-year-old woman) plus review of all previously published cases
studies.outcome: updated RUCAM causality score for hepatocellular/mixed liver injury
studies.result: Both cases scored 7 on updated RUCAM = 'probable' causal relationship between ashwagandha and liver injury; both resolved after discontinuation

verdicts.claim: Cortisol Reduction — strong evidence, large magnitude, 11 studies, 27.9% figure
verdicts.reason: The 27.9% figure is verified in the full text of Chandrasekhar 2012 (KSM-66, 600mg/day, 60 days) and reinforced by a 2024 meta-analysis of 9 RCTs (MD -2.58, significant). However, a separate crossover RCT in aging overweight men (Lopresti 2019, low-dose Shoden extract) found no significant cortisol effect — the claim should note this is dose/population-dependent, not universal.

verdicts.claim: Anxiety & Stress — strong evidence, large magnitude, 10 studies
verdicts.reason: Chandrasekhar 2012 (PSS -44% vs -5.5%, p<0.0001) and the 2024 9-RCT meta-analysis (PSS MD -4.72, HAS MD -2.19, both significant) directly substantiate this as one of the best-evidenced ashwagandha effects.

verdicts.claim: Sleep Quality — moderate evidence, moderate magnitude, 6 studies
verdicts.reason: A 90-day RCT (Gopukumar 2021, not separately detailed above but located in search) reported significantly improved PSQI scores; classification as 'moderate' rather than 'strong' is reasonable given this is typically a secondary rather than primary endpoint across trials.

verdicts.claim: Cognitive Function Under Stress — citing 'A 2019 RCT (Choudhary et al.)', 300mg twice daily, 8 weeks
verdicts.reason: The Choudhary trial matching this description (300mg BID, 8 weeks, WMS-III outcomes) is dated 2017, not 2019, and enrolled adults with diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MCI) — not the general healthy-adult population implied by the page. The underlying cognitive-benefit claim is directionally supported by other RCTs in genuinely healthy/stressed adults (Kale 2024, Leonard 2024), but the specific citation used on the page misattributes both the year and the study population.

doseAssessment.trialRange: 300-600mg/day of standardized root extract (KSM-66 or unbranded) is the dominant range across positive RCTs; Chandrasekhar 2012 (the source of the 27.9% cortisol figure) specifically used 600mg/day (300mg BID) of KSM-66.
doseAssessment.suggestedText: No change needed — 300-600mg/day accurately reflects the trial range, though the strongest cortisol evidence (Chandrasekhar 2012) sits at the top of that range (600mg/day), not the middle.

safetySignals.signal: Multiple published case reports/case series of ashwagandha-associated hepatocellular or cholestatic liver injury, including RUCAM-scored 'probable' causality; not currently disclosed in the page's side-effects list
Additional independent liver-injury case reports (jaundice, elevated transaminases, one requiring plasmapheresis) reported from Poland, UK, and in a multiple-sclerosis patient on natalizumab

Denmark's Veterinary and Food Administration (DVFA) banned ashwagandha food supplements in April 2023 citing inability to establish a safe dose, based on a 2020 DTU risk assessment flagging reproductive/hormonal/neurological safety concerns — discussed in a peer-reviewed commentary

gaps: The page's side-effects list omits the liver-injury signal entirely despite multiple published case reports/case series with 'probable' RUCAM causality scores.
The page's side-effects list omits the Danish/Nordic regulatory action, which is a material safety-context data point for consumers.

The core cognitive-effects citation (Choudhary) is mis-dated and mis-populated (MCI adults framed as a general finding); no equivalent-quality RCT in truly healthy, non-clinical adults with an 8-week single-extract design and this magnitude of effect was found.
No long-term (>90 day) continuous-use safety RCT data located; most trials run 8-12 weeks.
